scope: Target plan reconciliation only; no Mantle runtime/compiler/native implementation changed
principles: One core policy/algorithm owner across backends
One public array family; one owning device; operation targets independent of storage lifetime/ownership
Base.length/size query logical dimensions; Base.resize! mutates them
Native acceleration extends the same resource/region/command model; native eligibility is measured, not assumed
No backend-specific user code; dispatch on enabled device capabilities
Seek representations improving compilation and execution; prefer runtime when a measured tradeoff remains unavoidable
Simple stable types with bounded code/ABI specialization, not graph topology/resource identities/dynamic extents in types
Standard eager methods and known-function call! share one Mantle operation definition/recipe
Shared Mantle layer owns device/compiler/semantic/execution capability selection; backends report facts and encode commands
user_decisions_preserved: Explicit scratch request instead of lifetime hidden in a device constructor
Persistent device-owned state/retained leaves shared directly across nodes and same-array foreign imports
Canonical GPU logical size plus capacity and internal Cell/prepare machinery
No public size-cell handle or new dynamic-view/overflow abstraction
No speculative staged restore; retain F74 direct-host evidence and investigation threshold
additional_consistency_decisions: Known operation definitions/recipes supply shared validation, effects, returns, candidate materialization and resource management; arbitrary Julia capture is not promised.
Return contracts are explicit per operation definition: mul! returns C; recorded Array returns a typed future; neither ! nor a universal-future heuristic determines this.
Array(a) is standard blocking eager conversion; call!(target,Array,a) declares a snapshot; Readback(previous_future) only requests its next execution. No separate public eager Readback(array).
Actual CPU work during replay uses explicit HostCall staging/host cuts; unsupported call! never falls back to it or eager execution.

The core selector intersects enabled hardware/compiler capability, precision/layout/shape/alias/workspace and recording/control requirements, then compares eligible candidates using measured evidence.
Eager calls materialize immediately; graph compile materializes/reselects retained recipes; replay uses baked choices without probing/tuning.
KA.get_backend(a) stays the owning Mantle Device; ordinary host length/size queries synchronize and return snapshots, never a recording target or hidden graph provenance.

findings.title: Aliased transient reuse needs a DAG frontier, not one last topological user
findings.decision: Alias reuse follows all maximal old users and minimal new users; root spans and descriptor epochs use one shared frontier algebra.

contracts.section: 16.4 One command DAG and complete alias frontiers

acceptance: Two readers on distinct queues, with the earlier-listed reader deliberately delayed; poison/reuse the bytes in a later transient.
Remove one frontier edge as a negative control.

findings.title: Automatic acceleration updates do not cover a writer and trace in the same segment
findings.decision: Insert write -> matching build/refit -> AS-read edges inside a segment; accepted builds consume only covered dirty versions.
acceptance: One graph: deform -> query/trace; results match an independently rebuilt scene.
Build -> deform -> external trace.
Deform -> failing host/preparation stage before build; a later independent trace must see the required update.

findings.title: A GPU-length writer makes its repeated group illegal in the sketch
findings.decision: Infer device resize! effects, include internal prepares in controls, and validate/publish full declarations atomically.
acceptance: Repeat a compact/length-publish/consume chain through zero and nonzero counts.
Declare a length writer both before and after repeat!; failed declarations leave nodes and holds unchanged.

findings.title: A host semaphore timeout is incorrectly treated as proven device loss
findings.decision: WaitTimeout preserves pending work and holds; native failure alone establishes DeviceLost. Costs are estimates unless independently justified as bounds.
acceptance: Several individually short upstream segments exceed the downstream queue's deadline in aggregate without poisoning the device.
Actual disposable-context device-loss tests still verify quarantine.
Profile calibration cannot turn a feasible launch into an error claimed to be mathematically necessary.

findings.title: Reselection on growth has no operation-reconstruction step
findings.decision: Retain RegionNode recipes and stable outputs; materialization reselects the full command/workspace sequence.
acceptance: Growth across two candidate domains with different node counts/workspaces; compare fresh declaration versus recompile.
Code/config invalidation and tuning affect a subsequent compile according to one documented policy.

findings.title: Graph construction still silently chooses transient lifetime
findings.decision: Persistent by default on one owning Device; explicit scratch lifetime independent of constructor/operation target; graphs reference the same leaf directly, without adaptation.
acceptance: Recorded particle state survives replay and plan replacement.
A leaf retained by a second graph preserves allocation and size metadata.
An explicitly temporary array can be arena-aliased and cannot escape without a diagnosed lifetime transition.

findings.title: Native-array import has a qualification gate but no usable public entry
findings.decision: MantleArray(dev,foreign;copy=false,stream) imports allocation ownership/readiness and canonicalizes generation-aware aliases.

contracts.section: 16.6 Imported allocations and explicit device communication

acceptance: An existing CuArray enters a CUDA Mantle graph without copying.
Two wrappers/views over the same allocation cannot evade hazards.
Drop the external Julia handle while work is in flight; no early free; completion is safely handed back to the foreign stream.

findings.title: Conditional draws cannot correctly implement the cached shadow-pass example
findings.decision: Condition the complete clear+draw region; native control or a qualified core conditional-clear candidate resets active maps and preserves skipped maps.

contracts.section: 16.7 Conditional render reset and image subresources

acceptance: Render an occluder, remove/move it, dirty the shadow map; uncovered depth resets correctly.
A clean frame preserves the map and performs no update work.
Validate both outcomes on Vulkan and Metal.

findings.title: Missing Group propagation silently changes the meaning of model code
findings.decision: Known-function call!(Graph/Group,f,args...) lowers through the shared Mantle definition; library composition explicitly emits recorded calls/raw primitives. Arrays retain one Device and no recording context.
acceptance: A realistic recorded model with broadcast, matmul and device-output reductions repeats in full.
Reuse operands directly in sibling Groups/other graphs without device/type/identity changes.
Unknown functions reject before publication or eager execution; per-definition return tests include a ! function not returning its destination.

findings.title: Nested solver loops and reusable graph regions are forbidden
findings.decision: Nested Groups/loops and legal internal work compose; device-controlled HostCalls reject; native build controls require eligibility/equivalence.
acceptance: Timestep -> Newton -> CG/line search with independent GPU termination and correct state reset.
Compose an existing solver/model region into another graph or repeated region without rewriting its launches.

findings.title: Unrolling removes the representation needed for efficient native loops
findings.decision: Select native region encoding before portable bounded expansion; measure compile time, plan/slot bytes and stop overhead.
acceptance: Short early termination at a large maximum; compare CPU compile cost, GPU work and plan bytes.
Native and fallback encodings produce identical zero/one/many-iteration results and retain submission-budget semantics.

findings.title: Dependency construction retains quadratic access history
findings.decision: Bounded access frontiers replace quadratic historical-use accumulation; unknown composite overlap remains explicitly conservative.

contracts.section: 16.4 One command DAG and complete alias frontiers

acceptance: Long shared-resource chains and independent branches at increasing node counts.
Large material/plot sets and unrolled/native-loop variants; report edges, compile time and peak host memory.

findings.title: Blanket no-capture and kernel-only regions exclude useful library recordings
findings.decision: Allow capability-qualified closed library/communication recordings with explicit effects/workspaces; no consumer capture or second graph runtime.
acceptance: A caller-workspace cuBLAS candidate records/replays safely when supported.
A library recording with hidden allocations, unsupported host output or invalid conditional-body nodes is rejected before enqueue.

findings.title: Arena sharing is coupled to scheduling priority
findings.decision: Separate share_scratch from priority and use core logical queue lanes capable of same-kind endpoint mapping.

contracts.section: 16.4 One command DAG and complete alias frontiers

acceptance: Two independent equal-priority workloads with sufficient headroom versus memory-pressure mode.
An editor frame beside background compute; measure real overlap and latency instead of only host submit time.

findings.title: GPU-driven command streams cannot be expressed by changing draw count alone
findings.decision: Typed DrawCommand/DispatchCommand and ExecutionSet expose bounded GPU command streams, live counts and declared program/resource sets.

contracts.section: 16.8 Indirect streams and modern launch requirements

acceptance: GPU cull -> compact draw commands -> draw-indirect-count with heterogeneous mesh ranges.
GPU command ordering/pipeline selection where supported; no per-object CPU rerecord or host count download.

findings.title: Modern kernel execution features lack an explicit runtime contract
findings.decision: Reuse KI facts/intrinsics in the shared Mantle operation selector; intersect device/compiler semantics and launch/recording/control/workspace requirements once for eager and recorded candidates.

contracts.section: 16.8 Indirect streams and modern launch requirements

acceptance: One end-to-end optimized DNN kernel using asynchronous movement/tensor operations with descriptor/workspace lifetime checks.
A cooperative/cluster candidate is selected only with legal geometry/residency and cannot be arbitrarily split.
Retain F34 evidence; no claim that these primitives are wholly absent today.

findings.title: Whole-root and whole-plan hazards block disjoint resource work
findings.decision: Proven ranges/subresources and descriptor epochs refine canonical root uses; unknown overlap remains root-conservative.

contracts.section: 16.4 One command DAG and complete alias frontiers

acceptance: Disjoint views/pages overlap safely; overlapping or unknown mappings still order.
KV append with reads of independent regions; streamed upload/compute overlap; image mip/layer producer-consumer tests.

findings.title: Image API is narrower than the stated general GPU/raster scope
findings.decision: Typed image views and sampling/storage/atomic families have explicit format/dimension/usage requirements and separate native gates.

contracts.section: 16.7 Conditional render reset and image subresources

acceptance: Compute-generated image sampled by a following draw without a compulsory array-to-image workaround.
3-D/array/mip paths required by actual consumers; correct subresource hazards and descriptor retirement.
Picking/integer attachments, MSAA resolves, storage-image support and feedback qualification remain distinct.

findings.title: Recorded RNG semantics are not specified
findings.decision: Explicit RNG counter resources advance only executed work, survive recompile, reset explicitly and stay isolated from tuning.
acceptance: Successive replays advance samples; seeded replay from reset is reproducible within the promised scope.
Recompile and queue scheduling do not accidentally reset/reuse a stream.
Two sessions and repeated-body stochastic operations have intentional independent streams.

findings.title: FEM and general simulations are not first-class replacement consumer gates
findings.decision: Add actual FEM/particle and representative backward/update acceptance while preserving prior consumer baselines.
acceptance: A small independently checked FEM assembly/solve and convergence history.
A retained particle birth/death/contact timestep with GPU logical sizes.
Coupled simulation -> ray/raster display in one graph plus two-graph sharing.

findings.title: Multi-GPU LLM/solver execution is outside the current graph boundary
findings.decision: Explicit recordable transfers/collectives connect per-device graphs; retain synchronous devicecopy! and qualify peer/host-cut/participation protocols.

contracts.section: 16.6 Imported allocations and explicit device communication

acceptance: When this scope is enabled, two device graphs exchange device data without a mandatory host-sized snapshot and retain correct completion/ownership.
Collective participation and failure handling are qualified for the actual library/version.

findings.title: Readback appendix reintroduces the public Plan/record path and fixed-shape rebuild
findings.decision: Standard eager Array conversion and recorded call!(target,Array,a) share a snapshot recipe; graph outputs/pending requests are stable and Readback(previous_future) requests the same existing output next run.
acceptance: One public lifecycle example uses only final entry points.
Zero/nonzero GPU-sized snapshots and replay preserve coherent size/payload, or fail at the documented boundary.
Future teardown and prefailure accepted snapshots retain their existing lifetime guarantees.

findings.title: Multi-command recipes lose ordering when only barrier-shaped dependencies are emitted
findings.decision: Core lowers every internal command with identity/effects/edges; native region callbacks preserve a single core child walk.

contracts.section: 16.4 One command DAG and complete alias frontiers

acceptance: A multi-kernel build prefix and cell/data copy sequence on a DAG backend produce identical results to the linear backend.
Randomize independent native-node execution; removing an internal edge must fail a negative control.

findings.title: Producer writes need a bounded allocation view distinct from the old logical extent
findings.decision: Checked internal capacity descriptors support producers; final resize! publishes size, empty input publishes zero, no extra public metadata handle.
acceptance: A checked compaction output grows from logical zero within known capacity without requiring raw unchecked writes.
Publish/prepare ordering covers same-kernel producers, empty inputs and multi-kernel scatter chains.
